page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL processor cores operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Storage is bundled with a 614 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are present on this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the E16ds_v4 demonstrates consistent mid-range performance. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1244.0 and a multi-core score of 7658.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 830.49 GB/sec, which drops to 69.79 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 41.6 GB/sec. Database operations score 5749.22 on Passmark, and the instance processes 13.72 million Redis SET operations per second. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM inference workloads; while prompt processing for a small 135M model reaches 878.33 tokens/second, prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to a weak 29.49 tokens/second, indicating limitations for larger AI workloads.

The qualitative cost profile of the E16ds_v4 reflects its positioning as a memory-dense resource. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides high local storage capacity without requiring separate storage attachments, enhancing overall resource density. Given its high memory capacity and solid database benchmark performance, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and static web serving.
